title: Deterministic A/B Test Bucketing
hints: Don't use `hashValue` — it changes every launch.
FNV-1a: `hash ^= byte; hash = hash &* prime` over the UTF-8 bytes.
Bucket = `hash % 100`; walk cumulative split percentages to pick A, B, C…
jsBridge: Deterministic bucketing hashes `experiment:userID` with a stable hash (FNV-1a), because Swift's `Hasher` is reseeded every launch. JS has no randomised built-in hash, but the same stable-hash logic appears in every A/B SDK.

compass.q: A JS A/B SDK hashes user IDs with murmurhash. Why can't Swift use `hashValue` for the same job?
Changing the split from 50/50 to 90/10: do existing users switch buckets? Should they?
Client-side bucketing vs server-assigned variants: which works offline, and which is consistent across devices?
Why salt with the experiment name? What correlation bug happens without it?
